label: Wizardcraft
subject: arcana
title: ON THE CRAFT OF WIZARDS
subtitle: Wizards do not begin as wizards. Most come from dust, hunger, or bright accidents. The art is older than kingdoms and younger than fire.

sections.heading: DUST, HUNGER, AND ACCIDENTS
body: Wizards do not begin as wizards. They begin as children who stared too long at storms, as farmers who heard a voice in the furrows, as beggars who touched the wrong relic at the right moment.
Most come from dust, hunger, or bright accidents. The tower gathers them up like lost pages and tries to bind them into something that can be read without screaming.

sections.heading: WHAT WIZARDCRAFT IS
body: Wizardcraft is not a gift. It is a discipline sharp enough to cut its wielder.
The art is older than kingdoms and younger than fire. It remembers when people bargained with mountains and forgot their own names in return, and it has learned a few new tricks since.
At its heart, wizardcraft is the practice of persuading reality to reconsider itself for a moment.

sections.heading: TOOLS OF THE TRADE
list: Names – True, half-true, and the ones you wish were true. All of them have weight.
Circles – Not cages, but mirrors. They show magic what it is about to do and ask whether it is sure.
Lines of Force – Drawn in chalk, ash, blood, or breath. A wizard spends most of his life learning where not to draw them.
Cost – The only tool that never dulls. Every working leaves a mark somewhere; the craft is choosing where.

sections.heading: ON BREAKING THE RULES
body: Wizardcraft has rules, but they are written in pencil. Its rules change whenever someone disobeys them boldly enough and survives the correction.
The tower keeps careful note of such rebellions. Some become new standard practice. Others are filed under "Things Never To Attempt Again" and sealed with wax that never cools.

Your wizard will be tempted to improvise before he understands. That is how most tales of great mages begin—and how most of them end. Your task is to teach him which rules may bend and which were never rules at all, only warnings.
